title: Major Bob Khathing: The Great Tangkhul Patriot, Soldier, and Statesman of Tawang

Biography of Major Ralengnao 'Bob' Khathing, MC, Padma Shri
publisher: Tangkhul Scholars Association / NEFA Heritage Trust
subject: Biography (Jeevani), Military History & Statesmanship
notes: Authoritative biography of Major Ralengnao 'Bob' Khathing (1912-1990), legendary Tangkhul Naga soldier, recipient of Military Cross (MC), Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE), and Padma Shri. Chronicles his early life in Ukhrul, heroism in World War II, historic 1951 peaceful integration of Tawang, and service as Indian Ambassador to Burma.

front_matter.title_page: Major Bob Khathing: The Great Tangkhul Patriot, Soldier, and Statesman of Tawang (1995)
front_matter.preface: Major Ralengnao 'Bob' Khathing is celebrated as one of modern India's most extraordinary nation-builders. Born in Ukhrul, Manipur, on February 28, 1912, he became the first person from the hill tribes of Manipur to graduate from university (Cotton College, Guwahati). In World War II, he fought valiantly against the Japanese in Burma with V Force, winning the Military Cross. In February 1951, leading an Assam Rifles expedition through treacherous Himalayan snowfields, he peacefully established Indian civil administration over Tawang without firing a single shot. He later helped build the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), served as Chief Secretary of Nagaland, and was appointed India's Ambassador to Burma.

chapters.summary: Birth in Ukhrul, Christian mission schooling, Cotton College graduation, and early teaching career.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Ralengnao Bob Khathing February 28, 1912 zingsho eina Ukhrul ramli pharisaye. Awui ava Rubichon kala awui ava-va Tangkhul Christian community-wui respected leader-leisai. Ana Ukhrul mission school kala Shillongli lairik kaphāmei hanglaga, Cotton College Guwahati eina B.A. pass saye; a Manipur hill tribeswui ngachaili graduate khare mayarnao-sai. Ana Ukhrul high school-li headmaster salaga Tangkhul yaronaobingli education milaga nation-building-wui lambi chitheiye.
chapters.english_translation: Ralengnao Bob Khathing was born in Ukhrul, Manipur, on February 28, 1912. His parents were pioneer leaders of the early Tangkhul Christian church and education movement. After brilliant schooling in Ukhrul and Shillong, he graduated with a B.A. from Cotton College, Guwahati, becoming the very first university graduate among the hill tribes of Manipur. He returned to Ukhrul to serve as headmaster, inspiring generations of Naga youths toward educational excellence.

chapters.title: World War II Heroism & The Military Cross (1939-1945)
chapters.summary: Commissioned into the British Indian Army, commanding V Force guerillas behind Japanese lines, and Military Cross award.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: World War II phoklakha, Bob Khathingna British Indian Army-li commission khuiye. Ana 19th Hyderabad Regiment kala V Force guerilla unit command saye. Manipur kala Burma frontier-li Japanese forces-wui ngalemli ana heroic intelligence kala combat operations lead saye. Awui gallantry kala courage theilaga British Crown-na ali Military Cross (MC) kala MBE decoration miserie. A Tangkhul warrior pride-wui supreme symbol-sai.
chapters.english_translation: When World War II erupted, Bob Khathing was commissioned into the British Indian Army. He commanded the 19th Hyderabad Regiment and the elite V Force guerrilla unit behind Japanese lines. Operating across the rugged jungles of Manipur and the Burma frontier, he executed daring reconnaissance and combat operations. For extraordinary gallantry under fire, he was awarded the coveted Military Cross (MC) and the MBE, becoming a supreme symbol of Tangkhul martial valour.

chapters.title: The Historic Tawang Expedition of February 1951
chapters.summary: Leading 200 Assam Rifles troops across snow-bound Sela Pass to establish Indian administration over Tawang peacefully.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: February 1951-li Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru kala Sardar Patel-wui directive eina Major Bob Khathingna 200 Assam Rifles jawans lead saye. Athumna snow-covered Sela Pass (13,700 feet) cross salaga Tawangli vashukrie. Chithuili ana Monpa elders, Buddhist Monks kala Tawang Monastery Abbot eina diplomatic talks saye. Khikha bullet mashukla, ana Indian national flag Tawangli phungsangserie kala civil administration phokserie! Hi Indian geopolitical history-li greatest peaceful expedition hoda reot-kasaye.
chapters.english_translation: In February 1951, under strategic directives from New Delhi, Major Bob Khathing led an expedition of 200 Assam Rifles troops. Braving blizzards, they crossed the treacherous Sela Pass at 13,700 feet and entered Tawang. With consummate diplomatic tact, Khathing held parleys with Monpa village chieftains, head lamas, and the Abbot of Tawang Monastery. Without firing a single shot, he raised the Indian tricolour over Tawang and established civil administration, securing India's strategic northern border in one of the greatest peaceful military expeditions in modern history.

chapters.title: Ambassador to Burma, Statesmanship & Padma Shri (1951-1990)
chapters.summary: Founding the SSB, serving as Chief Secretary of Nagaland, Ambassador to Myanmar, and Padma Shri honor.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 4: Tawangwui tharan, Bob Khathingna Special Frontier Force kala SSB-li founding leader salaga ot sai. Ana Nagaland State-wui Chief Secretary salaga peace kala administrative stability phung-ungmi. 1972-li Government of India-na ali Ambassador to Burma (Myanmar) appoint saye; a first tribal diplomat from Northeast India hoda history sakahaye. President of India-na ali Padma Shri honor miserie. January 12, 1990 zingsho eina ana Mantripukhri Imphal-li shok-unglakna; awui ming Tangkhul kala India-wui history-li thot pupup ngashan-leisara!
chapters.english_translation: Following Tawang, Bob Khathing served as a foundational architect of the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB). He served as Chief Secretary of Nagaland, ushering in peace and administrative modernization during turbulent times. In 1972, the Government of India appointed him Ambassador to Burma, making him the first tribal diplomat from Northeast India to head a diplomatic mission abroad. He was conferred the national honor of Padma Shri. He passed away on January 12, 1990, in Imphal, leaving an immortal legacy of patriotism, courage, and integrity.

grammar_notes: Eulogistic memorial conclusion: 'thot pupup ngashan-leisara' (shall be remembered throughout all generations).
